note: A summary of published views from banks and industry bodies, not a recommendation. Forecasts are often wrong — use them as context alongside the chart.

Gold.headline: Pulling back after a strong run: record Chinese buying vs a Fed that has started raising rates again
Gold.context: Around US$4,370/oz on 22 Sep 2026 — down about 4% over the month but up about 18% over the year. It fell below US$4,300 briefly when the Fed raised rates on 16 Sep.
supportive: China imported more than 1,000 tonnes of gold in Jan–Aug 2026, already above its total for all of 2025
Central banks keep adding gold to diversify away from US-dollar assets
Chinese insurers may now hold up to 1% of assets in physical gold (roughly 200 tonnes of potential demand)
Ongoing geopolitical tension and long-term inflation worries
headwinds: The Fed raised rates on 16 Sep 2026 to 3.75–4.00%, its first hike since 2023; officials see about 4.1% by end-2026, held through 2027
Higher rates increase the cost of holding gold, which pays no interest
Western investor interest and gold ETF holdings have softened

forecasts.view: Q4 2026 average US$6,000/oz; 2027 average about US$6,263/oz (cut 4–13% from February)

sources.name: Yahoo Finance — Gold price today, 22 Sep 2026
INN — Gold drops below US$4,300 as Fed hikes

Silver.headline: Following gold with bigger swings, while solar demand softens
Silver.context: Traded mostly US$56–58/oz in June 2026. The gold/silver ratio is about 70, up from a low of 45 in January.
supportive: Tends to follow gold, so central-bank support for gold also helps silver
Still widely used in industry: electronics, solar and electrical parts
headwinds: Silver used in solar panels is expected to fall about 30% (around 60 million oz) as manufacturers use less of it
China is running down its stockpiles after an export tax rebate was removed; India has raised import duties
Rate hikes weigh on precious metals, and silver usually falls further than gold when gold dips

forecasts.view: Q4 2026 US$63/oz; 2026 average US$70; 2027 average about US$63.9; gold/silver ratio drifting toward 75

Platinum.headline: Supply still falls short of demand, but investors have been pulling money out
Platinum.context: Peaked near US$2,924/oz on 26 Jan 2026, then fell to about US$1,566 by 30 Jun.
supportive: The World Platinum Investment Council expects a 4th year in a row where demand exceeds supply (2026)
More than 60% of demand is industrial (car catalytic converters, chemicals, glass)
Most supply comes from South Africa, so disruptions there move the price
headwinds: Platinum ETFs saw about 700,000 oz of outflows in the first half of 2026
A strong US dollar and high Treasury yields

sources.name: WPIC — 2 to 5 year supply & demand view

Palladium.headline: Depends on car demand; the risk of a supply surplus caps the upside
Palladium.context: Hit US$2,195/oz on 26 Jan 2026, then fell to a nine-month low near US$1,177 in June.
supportive: Supply is concentrated in Russia and South Africa, so sanctions or outages can cause spikes
Hybrid cars still use palladium catalytic converters
headwinds: About 80% of demand comes from petrol-car exhausts; the shift to electric cars erodes it
Forecasters see a higher risk of supply exceeding demand than for platinum
